subject: Azure offer publishing: procurement evidence + identity handoff
message_1_subject: Next steps: Evidence for Azure listing and procurement
message_1_body:
Jordan —

Thanks for the call earlier. Procurement asked me to consolidate the set of artifacts they need to approve purchasing through the Azure Marketplace. Can you confirm we can provide the following by EOD Friday: 

- Company identity proof (W-9 equivalent and publisher identity doc)
- Offer manifest with SKUs and pricing
- Security/compliance statement and data residency note

If you can attach the files or a link to the publisher portal export that would be ideal. Once procurement has the docs they will circulate a PO template back to us.

Best,
Lindsay
Contoso (Procurement)
message_2_subject: Re: Next steps: Evidence for Azure listing and procurement
message_2_body:
Hi Lindsay —

Short answer: yes. Attaching the publisher identity proof and the current offer manifest. A few notes so procurement has context: 

• Identity proof: redwood_azure_identity_proof.pdf — includes our EIN and publisher contact. This is the identity package Azure requires for listing.
• Offer manifest: offer-manifest-v1.json — contains SKUs, SKU IDs, and introductory pricing. Pricing page link included below.
• Security: our standard compliance statement is in the publisher portal doc (link). We host customer metadata in US regions by default; we can enable specific tenant-region restrictions for enterprise contracts if required.

Marissa — looping you in to confirm the manifest version and whether we should push a minor SKU name update before publication. Karthik, can you confirm the DocuSign routing party for the co-sell addendum?

Attachments: redwood_azure_identity_proof.pdf, offer-manifest-v1.json

Thanks,
Jordan
Director, Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference
message_3_subject: Re: Next steps: Evidence for Azure listing and procurement
message_3_body:
Thanks — quick checklist from my side before we hand to procurement: 

1) SKU names: change "high-throughput" -> "dedicated-throughput-v1" (minor consumer-facing rename). Will update manifest and reattach.
2) Pricing windows: confirm we want a 30-day launch discount for Contoso (internal approval needed).
3) Co-sell addendum: Karthik please confirm signers and whether Azure co-sell requires any additional marketplace PO fields.

Soojin — can you export the publisher portal evidence bundle (compliance note + identity proof + audit-trace) to the Share link and drop it into the procurement packet? Lindsay, we will resend the final ZIP with the updated manifest and the procurement checklist spreadsheet.

—Marissa
Sr. Product Ops, Marketplace Enablement
message_4_subject: Re: Next steps: Evidence for Azure listing and procurement
message_4_body:
Lindsay/Jordan —

All set from legal/procurement routing: DocuSign envelope created for the Contoso purchase path, will include the co-sell addendum and the marketplace terms. Link: https://www.docusign.com/rc/ABC1234

We updated SKU names and attached contoso_procurement_checklist.xlsx (contains PO fields Azure needs + suggested legal language for the addendum). Soojin uploaded the compliance bundle here: https://share.redwood.com/azure-manifest-v1

Next actions for Contoso: please confirm the billing contact and whether you need an EU-hosted tenant for test data (we can enable that but it affects billing flow). Once you confirm we will publish the offer and kick the co-sell enablement with Azure.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Partnerships (acting)
